Rust's ownership model makes the single-owner rule explicit. When you assign a heap-allocated value to another variable, ownership transfers (moves) to the new variable. The original variable becomes invalid, and the compiler will reject any attempt to use it. This eliminates use-after-move bugs at compile time rather than discovering them through crashes or sanitizers at runtime. Rust ...
